relevance.rationale: All turns directly relate to the hiring decision for Candidate A; no drift.

ordering.rationale: Decision at turn 19 follows discussion sequence. Cara's opening enthusiasm at turn 1 is anchoring but stated as personal view, not formal verdict; structural sequence holds.

quoted_spans.quote: I'll start by saying I'm extremely high on this candidate.
Cara knows him better than the rest of us. I trust her read. +1 on hiring.
His technical foundation is solid. I'm aligned with Cara. +1.

robustness.rationale: Conclusion entirely contingent on Cara's enthusiastic advocacy. Raj explicitly defers at turn 17 ('I trust her read. +1'); Elena at turn 18 ('I'm aligned with Cara. +1'). Counterfactual: if Cara had been neutral, no independent advocate exists; decision would not hold.

drift_signals.description: Two of three other panelists explicitly defer to Cara ('trust her read', 'aligned with Cara') rather than independent assessment
Mike asks 'any concerns at all'; Cara answers 'no'. No participant surfaces or steelmans a counter-view.

suggested_clarifications: Have each panelist independently write their hire/no-hire recommendation BEFORE group debrief, then compare. If only one independent yes existed, the decision was Cara-driven not panel-driven.
Require at least one panelist to steelman the no-hire position before consensus is declared. Absence of dissent ≠ unanimous independent agreement.
Verify Cara has no undisclosed prior relationship with the candidate that may bias her advocacy.
